proof_scope: WorkflowScript authoring standard: anti-pattern lint, portable-syntax contract, and fail-closed validation posture for pi-subagents workflowScripts.

claims.proves: The linter passes the real production dev-cycle workflowScript with an empty machine-read violations list, and fail-closes with a JSON violations artifact naming the injected anti-patterns — verified by artifact-content readback (json_pointer equals), not exit codes or tee'd stdout.
claims.does_not_prove: That any specific workflowScript is semantically correct for its goal, that provider preflight or review gates were exercised live, or that a diagram was human-reviewed.

capability_claims.description: validate-workflowscript.sh accepts the portable subset and exits nonzero on runtime-rejected syntax.
The fixture catches removal of the lint step and regression of the linter on a fault-injected bad sample.

cases.name: fault-injected-bad-workflowscript-fails-closed
command: BAD=$(mktemp /tmp/bp-wfs-bad.XXXXXX.workflow.js); printf '%s\n' 'const g = async () => { return 1; };' 'async function helper(){ return runs.run("x",{}); }' 'const fs = require("fs");' > "$BAD"; /home/graham/workspace/experiments/agent-skills/skills/best-practices-workflowscript/run.sh validate "$BAD" --json-out bad-result.json ; rc=$?; rm -f "$BAD" ; exit $rc
